findings.text: Package tests directly fire the real repository shims, contaminating its ledger so --trusted can credit definitions Codex never invoked and violating Acceptance 2, Constraint 4, and the machine-quality principle.
findings.fix: Copy both shim trees and the recorder into a tmp_path repository and execute only those copies, as .claude/hooks/test_codex_hook_shims.py already does.

findings.text: The shim records fired before resolving its cwd-relative checker target, so invocation from a subdirectory records success even though no gate verdict is delivered and the station subsequently permits continuation.
findings.fix: Resolve every delegated target from the shim's own repository location and write the ledger only after establishing that the intended target can execute, with a regression test covering non-root cwd.

findings.text: The report says every test ran in fresh temporary directories and touched no existing data, contradicting the two real-repository shim executions and hiding the resulting ledger mutation from the user.
findings.fix: Correct the report after isolating the probes, or explicitly disclose the repository-ledger write and its cleanup evidence.

verdicts.notes: F1 fatal by consequence: the ordinary package gate can manufacture the exact evidence used to continue past the trust stop. F2 independently fatal: fired becomes a false operational-success signal. Did not run the suite (read-only sandbox; identified tests would mutate the repo).

findings.text: Two probes fire this repo's real .codex/hooks/*.sh shims with cwd=REPO; loom_record_fire.py resolves the ledger via __file__, so any pytest run including this file appends real lines to this repo's ledger and --trusted afterwards falsely reports those PostToolUse definitions fired.
findings.fix: Run the shims in a tmp_path scratch repo (copy the two .sh files plus loom_record_fire.py into tmp_path/.codex/hooks/), mirroring test_abuse_hook_trust_branch_end.py.

findings.text: Every thin shim writes the ledger line BEFORE the trailing exec, whose target resolves relative to cwd; a hook invoked from a non-root cwd crashes with no verdict yet reads fired forever after.
findings.fix: Record only after confirming the exec target exists at the resolved path (or resolve via $0's directory), and add the cwd caveat to codex-first-contact.md.

findings.text: 'Exit 0 means every definition has fired at least once — continue' has no caveat that exit 0 can be produced by a crashed, cwd-broken shim that delivered no verdict.
findings.fix: Add one sentence: a fired line proves the shim ran, not that its delegate succeeded; a check that should have blocked and did not is evidence the cwd assumption broke.

findings.text: Module docstring omits that the ledger append is unsynchronised across concurrent firings and why that is accepted (a lost line is a never false negative, never a forged fired).
findings.fix: Add one sentence to the docstring.

verdicts.notes: F1/F2 confirm the branch-end adversary's findings from source. external-surface-grounding PASS_WITH_NOTES: Codex' actual PostToolUse tool_name for apply_patch not verified live; the design does not depend on it. Acceptance 4 re-checked and holds.
